entities.summary: Je suis partout was a French newspaper founded by Joseph-Arthème Fayard, first published on 29 November 1930. It was placed under the direction of Pierre Gaxotte until 1939. Journalists of the paper included Robert Brasillach, Pierre-Antoine Cousteau, Lucien Rebatet, Alain Laubreaux, the illustrator Ralph Soupault, and the Belgian correspondent Pierre Daye. A right-wing publication initially connected to the Action française movement, Je suis partout evolved into an outright fascist publication. During the Nazi occupation of France, it became a collaborationist newspaper.
